newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada mine blast kills one, injures another.
newsitem.headline: Canada mine blast kills one, injures another.

text.p: One miner was killed and at least one more was injured in an underground explosion on Monday, Royal Canadian Mounted Police said.
"The explosion took the life of one miner and injured another," RCMP spokesman Gaston Leblanc told Reuters in a phone interview from Fredricton, New Brunswick.

The incident happened at the Heath Steel lead and zinc mine late in the afternoon north of Newcastle. The injured miner was taken to Miramichi Hospital but it was not known if the worker's injuries were life-threatening, Leblanc added.
The nursing supervisor at Miramichi Hospital declined comment. Heath Mine manager Herb Scott could not be reached.
"The cause of the explosion is under investigation. It happened late this afternoon. To my knowledge there's nobody trapped in the mine," Leblanc said.
The Canadian Press news agency reported that a sulphur blast 80 metres underground trapped about 35 workers.
